topic: Alpha Blending Enable and Blend Function
extracted_claim: Alpha blending is enabled via glEnable(GL_BLEND). The standard blend equation is: C_result = C_source * F_source + C_destination * F_destination. The standard function for alpha transparency is glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA) which multiplies source by its alpha and destination by (1 - source alpha). For separate RGB/alpha control use glBlendFuncSeparate.
implementation_relevance: HSE renderer does not currently support alpha blending. This knowledge enables transparent object rendering.

hse_symbol_grounding.notes: HSE has no blending support; this is new capability

document_reference: LearnOpenGL Advanced-OpenGL/Blending, 'Don't break the order' section
extracted_claim: For correct alpha blending, transparent objects MUST be drawn back-to-front (furthest first). Depth testing is unaware of transparency — transparent fragments write to the depth buffer normally, occluding objects behind them. The rendering order must be: (1) draw all opaque objects first, (2) sort transparent objects by distance from camera, (3) draw transparent objects in sorted order.
implementation_relevance: HSE would need a sorting step for transparent objects before draw calls.

hse_symbol_grounding.notes: HSE draws all primitives in insertion order, no sort step

extracted_claim: For textures that are either fully opaque or fully transparent (like grass), use the GLSL 'discard' command when alpha < threshold (typically 0.1). This avoids the sorting requirement entirely. Texture wrapping must be set to GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE to avoid alpha interpolation artifacts at borders.
implementation_relevance: Simpler path for particle effects and vegetation — no sort needed.

hse_symbol_grounding.notes: HSE fragment shaders do not use discard
